# GridDragScroll cancels mousedown, so a click on a grid moves no focus

## Context

`Neo.main.addon.GridDragScroll` (drag-to-scroll for grid bodies, on by default through `Neo.grid.ScrollManager#dragScroll`) listens to `mousedown` on every registered grid body with `capture: true` and, for a left button, calls `event.preventDefault()` "to prevent text selection" (`src/main/addon/GridDragScroll.mjs:253-255`). The default action of `mousedown` is not only the selection anchor — it is also the browser's **focus move** to the nearest focusable ancestor of the target. Cancelling it keeps DOM focus exactly where it was.

Observed in a consumer workspace whose dock panes host grids, then reproduced against the engine in a real Chromium (headless, 2026-09-02):

| gesture | expected | observed |
|---|---|---|
| click into a grid pane's empty viewport (no row under the pointer) | the pane's tab container gains focus, its focus-gated header actions (`showOnFocus`) reveal | `document.activeElement` is unchanged; no `focusin`, no `focusEnter`, the middle rail stays collapsed |
| a rail reveal is open, click into a grid pane's empty viewport | the reveal leaves — its `revealed-focused` state dismisses on `overlayFocusLeave` | the overlay root keeps focus, the reveal stays open |
| click on a ROW (control) | the grid View gains focus | it does — `grid.Body`'s row-click handler focuses the View programmatically, so a row click is unaffected by this defect |

The last row is the boundary of the defect: only a click that hits no row depends on the browser's default to reach the View. (An earlier draft of this ticket listed "Enter after a cell click mounts no editor" as a third symptom; the probe falsified that attribution — the View is focused after a cell click, the editing plugin's `Enter`/`Space` registry sits on it, and `Enter` on the editable cell mounts the editor. The report was a gesture mismatch, see Out of Scope.)

The selection concern the `preventDefault` was written for is already owned by CSS: `resources/scss/src/grid/Body.scss:22-23` sets `user-select: none` on `.neo-mouse-drag-scroll`, the class `ScrollManager` adds to the body for exactly this addon (#8911). A `mousedown` inside a `user-select: none` subtree starts no selection, so the JavaScript cancel is redundant belt-and-braces whose only remaining effect is the focus loss.

## The Problem

Every consumer of "the grid holds focus after a click anywhere in it" breaks silently for the empty-viewport case:

- **Focus-gated dock header actions** (`toolbar.Base#focusSubjectId` / reactive `containsFocus`, #17874, #18014): a grid pane never reveals its rail by a pointer click into its empty area — and short stores leave most of a pane empty.
- **Rail reveal dismissal** (`dashboard/dock/interaction/RevealStateMachine.mjs` — a click-born reveal is `revealed-focused` and leaves on `overlayFocusLeave`, `RevealOverlay.mjs:401`): clicking the empty area of a grid outside the overlay is not "moving on", the transient stays.
- **Keyboard navigation from an empty click**: arrow keys and the editing plugin's `Enter`/`Space` (registered on the View anchor) go to whatever was focused before.

Grid `View` is designed as the single focus anchor (`src/grid/View.mjs:36-41`: root `tabIndex: '-1'`, programmatically focusable, not tab-reachable), precisely so that a click anywhere in the grid focuses it via the browser's default. The addon defeats the design at the main-thread layer, below anything the App Worker can observe — the worker sees a `click` and a `mousedown`, never a `focusin`.

Reproduction (any grid with `dragScroll` on, i.e. every grid by default): focus a button outside the grid, click the grid viewport below its last row, then `document.activeElement` — it is still the button. Same in the Workstation app's grid panes.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/main/addon/GridDragScroll.mjs:346` — `bodyElement.addEventListener('mousedown', me.onDragStart, {capture: true})`; `:212` ignores non-left buttons; `:253-255` `if (event.type === 'mousedown') { event.preventDefault() }` before the monitor phase starts (`:257-285`). The drag itself only activates after `delay` (100 ms) AND `minDistance` (5 px) in `onMonitorMove` (`:292-302`) — so the cancel applies to every plain click, not to drags.
- `src/grid/ScrollManager.mjs:83` adds `neo-mouse-drag-scroll` to the body; `resources/scss/src/grid/Body.scss:22-23` → `user-select: none`.
- `src/grid/View.mjs:36-41` — the focus anchor contract (`tabIndex: '-1'`).
- `src/manager/Focus.mjs:149-173` — `focusin`/`focusout` are the only inputs; a cancelled mousedown produces neither.
- `src/main/DomEvents.mjs:591` — the engine's own global `mousedown` forwards without cancelling; the addon is the one place a grid `mousedown` default dies.

## The Fix

1. `src/main/addon/GridDragScroll.mjs`: remove the `mousedown` `preventDefault()` in `onDragStart`. Leave the touch path untouched (`touchmove` cancel at `:182` disables native scrolling, a different default). Document on the handler why the mousedown default must survive: it carries the focus move, and selection suppression is the CSS rule's job.
2. Guard the selection claim, not just the focus claim: a positive control asserts `window.getSelection().toString() === ''` after a real drag-scroll across cell text, so the removal cannot regress the reason the line was written.
3. Red-first component witness, real Chromium: fixture app `test/playwright/component/apps/grid-focus/` (a short grid whose viewport has empty space below its last row, a long grid whose viewport scrolls, an outside `<button>`), spec `test/playwright/component/grid/ClickFocus.spec.mjs`:
   - click the empty viewport below the last row → `document.activeElement` is the grid view; the view's `containsFocus` reads `true` through `Neo.worker.App.getConfigs` — **the red-first arm**;
   - click a cell → same (control: the programmatic row-click path, green before and after);
   - drag 160 px vertically inside the long viewport → the View scrolled AND selection is empty (positive control for the retained drag + the CSS rule);
   - click the outside button → `containsFocus` back to `false` (the leave path is unaffected).

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.main.addon.GridDragScroll#onDragStart` (`src/main/addon/GridDragScroll.mjs:210`) | this ticket | a left `mousedown` over a registered grid body keeps its default action; the drag still arms through the monitor phase | n/a — behavior removal | JSDoc on the handler | component witness arms 1–3 |
| `.neo-grid-body.neo-mouse-drag-scroll { user-select: none }` (`resources/scss/src/grid/Body.scss:22`) | #8911 (existing) | unchanged; becomes the sole owner of selection suppression | n/a | Body.scss comment | positive control (arm 3) |
| `Neo.grid.View` focus anchor (`src/grid/View.mjs:36`) | existing | unchanged; a pointer click into empty viewport now reaches it as designed | n/a | existing JSDoc | arm 1 |

## Decision Record impact

none — aligned with the grid View focus-anchor design already in `src/grid/View.mjs`; no ADR amended.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 `GridDragScroll#onDragStart` no longer calls `preventDefault()` for `mousedown`; the touch branch is unchanged.
- [ ] AC-2 Red-first component witness (`test/playwright/component/grid/ClickFocus.spec.mjs` + fixture app): a click on the empty viewport below the last row leaves `document.activeElement` on the grid view with `containsFocus === true` — red on `dev` before the fix; the cell-click arm is the control and stays green on both.
- [ ] AC-3 Positive control in the same spec: a real pointer drag inside the View still scrolls (`scrollTop` changes) and leaves `window.getSelection().toString()` empty.
- [ ] AC-4 The existing grid/dashboard component suites and the Workstation e2e arms that touch grids stay green (`npm run test-components`, `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationGridRepaintNL` and `WorkstationDragTextSelectionNL`).
- [ ] AC-5 Handler JSDoc states the contract: the mousedown default carries focus; selection suppression is the CSS rule's.

## Out of Scope

- A rail reveal that stays open when focus leaves the document into an **iframe** (observed in the same consumer workspace; a different mechanism — `focusout` without a following `focusin` — and a different owner, `manager.Focus` / the reveal machine). Separate ticket once reproduced against an engine fixture (`test/playwright/component/apps/dock-splitter` hosts an iframe pane).
- Inline cell editing in the consumer's grid — verified working on the current engine: a click on the editable tree cell selects it and `Enter` mounts the editor (`.neo-grid-editor` with a focused input); the reported "nothing happens" was the gesture — that grid maps double-click to opening the record by design, and a click alone only selects. No engine defect.
- The pointer-events migration of the drag sensors (#17889) — `GridDragScroll` is a main-thread addon outside the `DragDrop` sensor family.

## Avoided Traps

- **Focusing the view from the addon** (`bodyElement.focus()` on mousedown): moves focus policy into a main-thread addon and fights the browser's own fixup (nearest focusable ancestor), which already does the right thing once the default survives.
- **Cancelling `mousemove` instead**: `preventDefault` on `mousemove` does not stop a selection that a mousedown started; the CSS rule is the correct owner, and it is already there.
- **Cancelling only once the drag activates**: the click (no drag) is exactly the case that needs the default, and the drag case is already covered by `user-select: none` — nothing is left for a late cancel to do.
- **Reading the cell-click arm as the witness**: it is green before the fix because the grid focuses the View itself on a row click; only the empty-viewport arm isolates the browser default.
